title: The Register That Packs Three Things: Reading a Sensor Chip's Bytes Without Guessing

questions.question: A 12 bit sensor reading of 0xFFF is read as an unsigned number. What does a driver think it is?
options: 4095, the far end of the range, when the reading was -1
questions.explanation: The joint resting just below level looks as if it is at full scale.

questions.question: How do you take a 2 bit field from bit 4 of a register?
options: (reg >> 4) & ((1u << 2) - 1u), shifting the field down and masking what is above it

questions.question: How is a 12 bit two's complement number made into an int?
options: Keep the low 12 bits, and if the top one is set subtract 2 to the twelfth: 0x800 becomes -2048 and 0xFFF becomes -1

questions.question: The chip holds a 12 bit reading in the top of two bytes. What must a driver do before sign extending?
options: Shift the 16 bit word right by 4, so the reading is in the low twelve bits
questions.explanation: Skipping it makes the reading sixteen times too big.

questions.question: What does an overrun flag mean for the frame that carries it?
options: The frame is good and an earlier one was lost, so it should be used and the loss recorded: it carried 0.1953 g in the test
questions.explanation: Throwing it away loses a good reading as well.

questions.question: Why do the tests pack frames by hand?
options: So the check is of the decoder against the chip's side of the wire and does not use the code it is checking: all 16384 frames decoded with no axis wrong
questions.explanation: A test that shares the code under test shares its bugs.
